title: About me
text:
Interests
I’m especially interested in (morpho)syntactic phenomena such as non-canonical passive constructions and long-distance dependencies. My work is mainly focused on German and tries to combine descriptive approaches, empirical evidence, and minimal-generative perspectives. In my dissertation and as part of my work in project A01 (), I explore whether exceptional extraction from islands can be explained by analogy. My PIs and supervisors are Jutta M. Hartmann and András Bárány.
I’m also interested in historical linguistics and language change – in particular, in questions such as what motivates grammaticalization processes and how these can be modeled syntactically.






Me talking about non-canonical passives at ConSOLE33, Göttingen.

About me
My name is Fabian Zöfelt ([ˈfabiːan ˈtsœfɛlt]). I’m a linguist and PhD student at Bielefeld University. Currently, I’m working in the project  Creativity in (morpho)syntactic variation. The role of analogy at  CRC 1646: Linguistic Creativity in Communication.
I’m especially interested in (morpho)syntactic phenomena such as non-canonical passive constructions and long-distance dependencies. My work is mainly focused on German and tries to combine descriptive approaches, empirical evidence, and minimal-generative perspectives. In my dissertation and as part of my work in project A01, I explore whether exceptional extraction from islands can be explained by analogy. My PIs and supervisors are Jutta M. Hartmann and András Bárány.
I’m also interested in historical linguistics and language change – in particular, in questions such as what motivates grammaticalization processes and how these can be modeled syntactically.
